summary: kemiljk ranked first. Its skills treated messy data and edge cases as part of the design: long client names wrap, missing ledger values read 'No due date' or 'Not tied to a project', the total notes 'net of 1 credit', and the benchmark showed no meaningful cost. taste came a close second with the most complete visual rethink, a sidebar app shell and a header summary that leads with what needs attention, and it was the only variant with no sampled contrast failures in either theme; a clipped Add button and truncated phone amounts held its fidelity score down. skills and ui-craft followed, with ui-craft drawing the accessibility judge's top rank but losing points for a phone layout that is 895px wide in a 390px viewport. The systems that helped this app most were rule sets about content, semantics and layout that the agent applied to the existing shadcn components, while motion-only skills (feel-better, emil, uiwiki) left the page looking and scoring like the baseline. The libraries cost the most: Fluid Functionalism added about 108 KB of gzipped JavaScript at load and lost input borders and the phone grid, Magic UI added about 54 KB of JavaScript for effects judges did not count as improvements, and the libraries.dev effects raised blocking time from about 1 s to about 23 s and kept roughly a third of the main thread busy at idle. For a working app UI, start with a content and behavior skill such as kemiljk or skills, add a visual-direction skill like taste if the product needs a new look, and check the phone layout and font weight it adds before shipping.
method: One Fieldwork page (React, Tailwind and default shadcn/ui) was rebuilt eleven times, each by a separate AI agent that read only one system's documentation. Three blind judges, a product designer, a design engineer and an accessibility and UX-writing specialist, scored anonymized builds on five axes against the unchanged baseline at 3. Performance was measured in headless Chromium with a 4x CPU throttle and no GPU and scored relative to the baseline.

groups.label: Rule skills: visual direction
groups.note: Changed tokens, type, layout and copy across the whole page. Biggest visible gains, and the only rule skills that introduced layout bugs.

groups.label: Rule skills: content, behavior and accessibility
groups.note: Kept the baseline look and worked on copy for edge cases, field-error semantics, task-row structure and focus. No added dependencies and no measurable performance cost.

groups.label: Rule skills: motion and polish
groups.note: Added list transitions, reorder motion or a wizard progress bar. Judges saw these pages as baseline with small additions.

groups.label: Component library
groups.note: Replaced shadcn components with the library's own. Largest change, and the only system all three judges ranked last.

groups.label: Effect packs
groups.note: Added animated and decorative components on top of the baseline. Judges saw no improvement, and both cost performance.

kemiljk.verdict: The strongest content pass in the test. It handles every messy ledger case in plain language and adds a skip link, clear 2px focus outlines and a Clear filters action without breaking anything. Its weak spots are reduced motion, which it does not honor, and reorder and sort, which have no positional motion.
kemiljk.bestFor: Data-heavy app screens with messy, real content
highlights: Ledger: long client names wrap, an Invoice column, 'net of 1 credit' total, overdue figure in red
Missing values read 'No due date', 'Not tied to a project', 'Set when sent'
Tabs show counts and the wizard shows a 'Fill in the required fields' hint
Failed-save state with a clear inline error and Retry
issues: Reduced motion not honored; about 12 long animations still run
Wrapped client names make very tall ledger rows on phone, and top-nav search squeezes to 'Search p' at 390px
Small muted counts measure about 4.35:1 in the light theme
kemiljk.effort: small (17 files, about 800 lines changed), no new dependencies
improve: Pair it with a motion skill and ask the agent to add a prefers-reduced-motion path for every animation it adds.
Set a line-clamp or a minimum column width for very long names on narrow screens, and give the nav search a fixed minimum width.
Darken the muted text token slightly so small counts clear 4.5:1.

taste.verdict: The most complete redesign: a sidebar app shell, a header summary that names what is at risk or overdue, grouped settings and restrained status color in both themes. It has the cleanest contrast and full reduced-motion support, but it introduces two layout bugs. Two judges ranked it in the top two and the design engineer ranked it third.
taste.bestFor: Giving an app a new, coherent visual direction
highlights: Sidebar shell and a header summary that leads with at-risk and overdue items
Ledger header reads '14 entries · 3 overdue' with the total owed
280ms FLIP reorder and zero-duration motion under reduced motion
Phone ledger tucks the project under the client name
issues: Task Add button overflows its card by about 20px at 1280px
Phone ledger amounts clip to '$1,...' and need horizontal scroll
Retry in the failed-save state reads as plain text
taste.effort: medium (30 files), adds IBM Plex Sans and Mono (about 84 KB of fonts downloaded; 570 KB shipped across all subsets)
improve: Check every changed card at 1280px and 390px before accepting; the Add button and the phone ledger both needed a second pass.
Give tables a phone layout (stacked rows or a hidden secondary column) instead of clipping amounts.
Style inline actions like Retry as buttons or links so they read as clickable.

skills.verdict: A careful refinement of the baseline with the best-calibrated list motion. Task metadata moves under the title so phone rows stay readable, long names wrap, and errors are linked to their fields. The accessibility judge ranked it lower, fifth, citing the always-enabled Next button and missing reduced-motion handling on some animations.
skills.bestFor: Polishing behavior and list interactions without a redesign
highlights: Task rows with metadata under the title, readable on phone
150ms FLIP on move and sort that switches to fades under reduced motion
Skip link and actionable error copy ('Enter the full email address, like billing@client.com')
Wizard Next marks invalid fields and focuses the first one
issues: Next looks enabled while the form is invalid
Some 2000ms animations still run under reduced motion
skills.effort: medium (28 files, about 340 lines changed), no new dependencies
improve: Keep Next disabled-looking until the step is valid, or keep it enabled and say so in a hint, but don't mix the two.
Add a reduced-motion pass for its longer animations.
Combine with a visual-direction skill if the product needs a new look; on its own it keeps the baseline style.

ui-craft.verdict: Strong desktop polish and the best accessibility work in the test: a numbered wizard stepper, inline hints, linked field errors, solid 2px focus rings and full reduced-motion support. The phone layout is broken, which pulled its fidelity score below baseline. The accessibility judge ranked it first; the other two ranked it fourth.
ui-craft.bestFor: Form guidance, error copy and accessibility on desktop
highlights: Numbered wizard stepper with next-step hints and an error icon
Ledger total labeled 'Total · all 14 entries' with credits and negatives clearly marked
Consistent 2px focus rings
No-results empty state that tells you how to recover
issues: Page is 895px wide in a 390px phone viewport (horizontal scroll)
Sort icons removed from all but the active column header
Sections lose their h2 headings
ui-craft.effort: medium (26 files, about 400 lines changed), adds Instrument Sans; slower interaction response in the benchmark (INP 744 ms vs 392 ms)
improve: Test at 390px: one wide element pushes the whole page to 895px. Find it with a layout check before shipping.
Keep sort icons visible on every sortable column so people can see which columns sort.
Restore section headings (h2) so the page structure works for screen readers.

ibelick.verdict: Looks like the baseline but improves semantics and number formatting. Field errors use role=alert and aria-describedby, the discard prompt is an alertdialog, and the disabled Next explains how to continue. The accessibility judge rated it above baseline; the other two saw no visual change.
ibelick.bestFor: Semantic and copy fixes with minimal visual change
highlights: Ledger hours aligned to two decimals (9,512.00) and a 'Total for 14 entries' label
Wizard hint 'To continue, enter a valid billing email'
Heading structure and alertdialog for discard
issues: Task titles truncate to a few characters on phone ('Send cat…')
Dark-theme At risk, Overdue and Delete badges remain about 2.89:1
ibelick.effort: small (19 files, about 235 lines changed), no new dependencies
improve: Let task titles wrap to two lines on phone instead of truncating.
Raise the dark-theme badge colors to at least 3:1 against their background.
Run it alongside a visual skill; it fixes semantics but changes little you can see.

uiwiki.verdict: Near-baseline with a few targeted additions: a wizard progress bar with 'Step 1 of 3', monospace invoice IDs and wrapping task titles. Remove is shortened to 250ms, and reorder and sort have no motion.
highlights: Wizard progress bar with 'Step 1 of 3'
Task titles wrap instead of truncating
Monospace invoice IDs in the ledger
issues: Stepper wraps awkwardly at 390px ('Step 1 of / 3')
Adds an 'Interface sounds' setting the product did not ask for
Reduced motion not honored; dark badge contrast unchanged at about 2.89:1
uiwiki.effort: medium (25 files, about 310 lines changed), no new dependencies
improve: Tell the agent to skip product features the rules suggest but the product doesn't need, such as the sounds setting.
Make the stepper label one unit ("Step 1 of 3") that doesn't break across lines.
Add reduced-motion handling and fix the dark badge contrast.

feel-better.verdict: Visually the baseline with slight spacing and type tweaks. It adds a blur-and-translate enter and exit on task add and remove that drops out under reduced motion, and links errors on two fields. Nothing broke.
feel-better.bestFor: Light motion polish on add and remove
highlights: Task add and remove animate in and out, and stop under reduced motion
Errors linked to two inputs via aria-describedby
issues: Three 400ms fade-in-up animations re-run alongside every sampled action
Reorder has no motion
feel-better.effort: medium (22 files, about 175 lines changed), no new dependencies
improve: Scope entrance animations to elements that actually changed so they don't replay on every action.
Add positional motion for reorder and sort if list movement matters to the product.
Use it as a finishing pass after a content or visual skill, not as the main system.

emil.verdict: Visually identical to the baseline, with under 0.5% of pixels differing. Its contribution is motion: a 250ms FLIP on reorder and sort with fade-only fallbacks under reduced motion, plus errors linked on two fields.
highlights: 250ms FLIP when tasks move or the list is sorted
Fade-only path under reduced motion
issues: Side panel still takes 500ms to enter
emil.effort: small (20 files, about 240 lines changed), no new dependencies
improve: Shorten the side panel's enter to about 300ms for a work tool; keep the longer timing for marketing surfaces.
Pair it with a content or accessibility skill; its motion work is solid but judges saw few visible changes.

magicui.verdict: The page looks like the baseline. Blur-fade section reveals, KPI number tickers and a hover spotlight on project cards are the visible additions, and 600ms add and remove animations made the task list feel slow to the design engineer. It runs more animations under reduced motion than the baseline and adds JavaScript weight.
magicui.bestFor: Marketing-style entrance effects, not app screens
highlights: KPI values count up from 0, with the final value available to screen readers
Cursor-following spotlight on project cards
issues: 600ms add and remove animations are slow for a work tool
19 animations under reduced motion versus 13 in the baseline
magicui.effort: small (9 files, about 490 lines added), adds motion and next-themes (+54 KB gzipped JS, LCP 2144 ms vs 1404 ms)
improve: Use its components only where motion helps people follow a change, and keep durations under about 300ms in app screens.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion in every component you add; some don't by default.
Budget for motion's extra JavaScript or load the effects lazily.

libraries.verdict: Outside the assistant panel the page is pixel-identical to the baseline; judges saw only a new AI avatar. The effects behind it are expensive: blocking time rose from about 1 s to about 23 s, the 95th-percentile frame from 33 ms to 83 ms, and about 34% of the main thread stays busy at idle. Field errors remain unlinked to their inputs.
libraries.bestFor: Isolated showcase effects where performance does not matter
highlights: Thinking orbs and a border beam on the assistant's waiting state
Generated bot avatar in the chat panel
issues: Total blocking time about 22.9 s vs 1.0 s baseline, and about 34% main-thread CPU at idle
Field errors have no aria-describedby
Raises the simulated assistant reply wait from 1.6 s to 3.2 s to fit the package's rules
libraries.effort: small (7 files, about 180 lines changed), adds border-beam, bot-avatars, img-fx, liquid-gooey, thinking-orbs, three and voice-glow (+251 KB gzipped JS)
improve: Keep these effects off everyday app screens; use them on a landing page or a showcase where they can run alone.
Pause canvas effects when they're off screen or the tab is idle to cut the idle CPU.
Don't change product behavior (like the reply delay) just to make an effect fit.

fluid.verdict: All three judges ranked it last. Swapping in the library's components gave fast 80ms transitions, dot status badges and good failed-save copy, but inputs lost their borders, the delete action lost its destructive color, settings labels were rearranged, and the phone project grid stays at three columns. It also adds the most JavaScript of any rule set or library apart from libraries.dev.
fluid.bestFor: New projects built on the library from the start
highlights: Dot-style status badges in the ledger and on project cards
Snappy 80ms transitions and a sliding tab indicator
Failed-save message with a clear title and Retry
issues: Fixed Nov 5: text fields had no visible boundary at rest (by design), so form fields read as plain text (WCAG 1.4.11)
Phone project grid stays three columns at 390px and titles break per word (CardGroup takes a fixed column count)
Fixed Nov 5: Delete was neutral gray (no destructive variant). Still open: reduced motion not honored; several focus stops lack a visible ring
fluid.effort: large (50 files, about 13,000 lines changed), adds Base UI, 10 Radix packages, motion and Inter Variable (+108 KB gzipped JS at load, 71 KB of fonts downloaded, LCP 2236 ms vs 1404 ms). pdf.js is also bundled but only loads when someone attaches a PDF.
improve: Start a new project on the library rather than swapping it into an existing shadcn app; most problems came from mixing the two.
Pick CardGroup's column count from the screen width (it takes a fixed number), so phone cards don't squeeze into three columns.
Set color-scheme on :root and .dark: the destructive button's light-dark() colors don't resolve without it. Then check reduced motion and every focus ring.
fluid.update: Nov 5 update: the creator shipped fixes for this feedback. Text fields now show a hairline at rest, Button has a destructive variant (used for Delete and Discard), and File Thumbnail can use a self-hosted pdf.js worker. The Compare view shows the updated build; the scores above are from the original blind judging.
